overview:
Maven is a veteran expert network platform founded in 2010 by Wyatt Nordstrom and Mark Platosh in San Mateo, California. One of the early technology-forward entrants in the expert network space, Maven built a platform that goes beyond traditional one-on-one expert calls to include online surveys, virtual roundtables, consulting projects, talent management solutions, and client discovery programs.

Maven has raised approximately $7.8 million in venture funding across four rounds, with investors including Accel and SuRo Capital. The company reached its Series A in January 2017. While smaller than industry giants like GLG or AlphaSights, Maven has carved out a niche through its diverse service portfolio and flexible engagement models that accommodate everything from single expert calls to ongoing consulting relationships.

The platform serves a range of clients including corporate strategy teams, investors, and consulting firms, with particular strength in technology and healthcare sectors. Maven's 65,000+ expert network is smaller than the largest players but is actively curated for relevance across its core verticals.

history.narrative:
Wyatt Nordstrom and Mark Platosh founded Maven in 2010, entering the expert network market during a period of significant growth and increasing institutional adoption. The company was among the first to take a technology-forward approach to expert networking, building a platform that could support multiple engagement formats beyond traditional phone consultations.

Maven raised its first funding — $1M from business angels and Accel — in 2010. A $2M round from SuRo Capital followed in 2012. The company completed its Series A in January 2017, bringing total funding to approximately $7.8M. Since then, Maven has continued to grow organically, focusing on diversifying its service offerings and deepening its expert network across technology, healthcare, and financial services.

servicesDetailed.name: Expert Consultations
servicesDetailed.description: One-on-one phone consultations connecting clients with vetted industry experts across technology, healthcare, financial services, and other sectors. Maven handles sourcing, scheduling, and compliance for each engagement.

servicesDetailed.name: Online Surveys
servicesDetailed.description: Quantitative survey research distributed through Maven's expert network, enabling clients to gather structured insights from targeted professional audiences across industries.

servicesDetailed.name: Virtual Roundtables
servicesDetailed.description: Group discussions bringing together multiple experts for moderated conversations on specific topics, providing clients with diverse perspectives in a single session.

servicesDetailed.name: Consulting Projects
servicesDetailed.description: Extended engagement format where experts provide ongoing advisory support for projects requiring deeper, sustained involvement beyond a single consultation.

servicesDetailed.name: Talent Management Solutions
servicesDetailed.description: Leveraging Maven's expert network for talent-related services including executive search support, industry hiring insights, and workforce advisory.

servicesDetailed.name: Client Discovery Programs
servicesDetailed.description: Programs connecting product and marketing teams with industry experts for customer discovery, market validation, and go-to-market research.

aiPlatform.narrative: Maven was one of the early expert networks to adopt a technology-forward approach, building its platform to support natural language project briefs and automated expert matching. The platform uses AI to parse client requests, identify relevant experts from the 65,000+ database, and rank matches by relevance and availability. Smart scheduling automates the logistics of expert engagement, reducing the friction typical of manual expert network operations.

clientFit.narrative: Maven is best suited for clients who need diverse research formats — not just expert calls, but surveys, roundtables, and consulting projects. The platform's flexibility makes it appealing for corporate strategy teams, product managers, and investors who need multiple engagement types. Clients requiring the deepest expert pools or the most institutional-grade compliance may prefer larger networks.
